key_insight: Everyday interactions with AI systems can change how people see themselves and reorganize their social networks, shifting relationships, norms of trust, and patterns of influence.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in understanding the socio-cognitive and network-level consequences of human–AI interaction, which hinders responsible design and deployment of AI that affects identity and social ties.
method: Mixed-methods approach combining behavioral experiments and self-report measures to track changes in self-concept after AI interaction.
Longitudinal social-network analysis of communication and tie strength before and after sustained AI exposure.
Interaction log and qualitative interview analysis to link specific AI features/behaviors to downstream social and psychological effects.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners this paper highlights the need to evaluate models not only on task metrics but also on social and psychological outcomes, informing design choices, evaluation protocols, and safeguards that preserve healthy social dynamics.
visual_elements: Before-and-after social network graphs showing tie formation, dissolution, and shifts in centrality
Timeline or flowchart illustrating progressive changes in self-concept and behaviors following AI interactions
Sankey/chord diagram mapping how interactions with different AI features redirect social attention and influence
Icon set (human, AI agent, survey, network node) to quickly convey methods and measured outcomes
paper_title: Human–AI interactions reshape the self and our social networks
paper_authors: Andreia Sofia Teixeira, Sukhwinder Singh Shergill, Guy Laban
